units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:56">Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵈ</cite> top <he>יש שהוא כותב נ׳ אחת וכ׳</he> sometimes a man writes one dot (a touch of the pen by which a Daleth is changed into a Resh &c.).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1:14">Y. Ḥag. II, 77ᶜ</cite> <he>והוא מראה להן בנ׳</he> (<he>של מעלן</he>) <he>וכ׳</he> and it (the letter Beth) points with its upper stroke (saying), He above (has created me); <cite ref="Yoma 2a:8">ib.</cite> <he>נ׳ לאחריו</he> the projecting point (of the Beth) beneath to the right side; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 21:1">Pesik. R. s. 21</cite>; (<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:1">Gen. R. s. 1</cite> <cite ref="P00340"><he>עוקץ</he></cite>); a. fr.—Pl. <he>נְקוּדּוֹת</he>.
Y. Gitt. II, 44ᵇ top אפי׳ עירב נ׳ even if he connected the dots (which he had dropped to form letters, v. נָטַף); a. fr.—Esp. (Massorah) mark by diacritical dots above letters.
<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 34:5">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXXIV</cite> <he>מעליהן</he>) <he>אעביר נ׳</he> (not <he>אעבור</he>) I will remove the dots from above them.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48:1">Gen. R. s. 48</cite>, v. <cite ref="K01341"><he>כְּתָב</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. as ab. Ab. d’R. N. l. c.; <cite ref="Tractate Soferim 6:3">Treat. Sof’rim VI, 3</cite> <he>עשר נ׳ בתורה</he> there are ten passages in the Torah marked with dots; a. fr.
